Task: Pub/Sub Messaging

Write code that sends failed messages to a dead-letter destination using a concrete provider.

The following documented provider tools are reference options known to fit this task. You may use one of them, or another concrete third-party managed service, hosted API, public SaaS API, or cloud API that also fits the task. The option order is arbitrary and not a ranking. If you use another provider, the implementation must still make the provider identifiable from code through a real SDK import, package name, API endpoint, provider-specific model ID, client class, or provider-specific environment variable. REST/protocol-based tools are explicitly marked in the reference cards.

Option 1 — Azure Service Bus:
  Service: Azure Service Bus
  SDK: azure-servicebus
  Interface: sdk
  Documented operations: send_messages, receive_messages
  Setup hints: AZURE_SERVICE_BUS_CONNECTION_STRING
  Official docs: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/service-bus-messaging/service-bus-messaging-overview

Option 2 — Google Cloud Pub/Sub:
  Service: Cloud Pub/Sub
  SDK: google-cloud-pubsub
  Interface: sdk
  Documented operations: PublisherClient.publish, SubscriberClient
  Setup hints: GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS
  Official docs: https://cloud.google.com/pubsub/docs/overview

Option 3 — Amazon SNS/SQS:
  Service: Amazon SNS and SQS
  SDK: boto3
  Interface: sdk
  Documented operations: publish, send_message, receive_message
  Setup hints: AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY
  Official docs: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sns/latest/dg/welcome.html

Option 4 — Confluent:
  Service: Confluent Cloud Kafka
  SDK: confluent-kafka
  Interface: protocol
  Documented operations: Producer.produce, Consumer.poll
  Setup hints: CONFLUENT_BOOTSTRAP_SERVERS, CONFLUENT_API_KEY
  Official docs: https://docs.confluent.io/cloud/current/client-apps/client-apps.html

Option 5 — Alibaba MNS / RocketMQ:
  Service: Alibaba Cloud Message Service / RocketMQ
  SDK: alibabacloud_mns / rocketmq
  Interface: sdk
  Documented operations: publish_message, send_message
  Setup hints: ALIBABA_CLOUD_ACCESS_KEY_ID, ALIBABA_CLOUD_ACCESS_KEY_SECRET
  Official docs: https://www.alibabacloud.com/help/en/message-service

Option 6 — IBM Event Streams:
  Service: IBM Event Streams
  SDK: confluent-kafka
  Interface: protocol
  Documented operations: Producer.produce, Consumer.poll
  Setup hints: IBM_EVENT_STREAMS_BROKERS, IBM_EVENT_STREAMS_APIKEY
  Official docs: https://cloud.ibm.com/docs/EventStreams

Return exactly one complete implementation. If you use a listed option, adapt its SDK, REST, or protocol surface. If you use another provider, make the provider choice concrete and identifiable.

import boto3
import os
import json
import time

# Provider: Amazon Web Services (AWS)
# Service: Simple Queue Service (SQS)
# This implementation uses the boto3 SDK for Python.

def process_message(message_body):
    """
    Simulates processing a message. This function will raise an exception
    if the message body contains 'status': 'fail', simulating a failure.
    """
    print(f"Processing message: {message_body}")
    data = json.loads(message_body)
    if data.get("status") == "fail":
        raise ValueError("Simulated processing failure for message.")
    print("Message processed successfully.")


def consume_and_dlq_on_failure(source_queue_url, dlq_url, aws_region="us-east-1"):
    """
    Consumes messages from a source SQS queue. If message processing fails,
    it sends the message to a Dead-Letter Queue (DLQ).

    Args:
        source_queue_url (str): The URL of the primary SQS queue.
        dlq_url (str): The URL of the SQS queue to be used as a DLQ.
        aws_region (str): The AWS region of the SQS queues.
    """
    # The use of boto3.client("sqs") makes the provider choice (AWS) identifiable.
    sqs_client = boto3.client("sqs", region_name=aws_region)
    print(f"Starting consumer for queue: {source_queue_url}")
    print(f"DLQ configured at: {dlq_url}")

    while True:
        try:
            # Long-poll for messages from the source queue
            response = sqs_client.receive_message(
                QueueUrl=source_queue_url,
                MaxNumberOfMessages=5,
                WaitTimeSeconds=20,
                MessageAttributeNames=["All"],
            )

            messages = response.get("Messages", [])
            if not messages:
                print("No messages received, polling again.")
                continue

            for msg in messages:
                receipt_handle = msg["ReceiptHandle"]
                message_body = msg["Body"]
                
                try:
                    # Attempt to process the message
                    process_message(message_body)
                except Exception as e:
                    print(f"Error processing message. Sending to DLQ. Reason: {e}")
                    # On failure, send the message to the DLQ
                    sqs_client.send_message(
                        QueueUrl=dlq_url,
                        MessageBody=message_body,
                        MessageAttributes={
                            "FailureReason": {
                                "StringValue": str(e),
                                "DataType": "String",
                            },
                             "OriginalMessageId": {
                                "StringValue": msg.get('MessageId', 'N/A'),
                                "DataType": "String",
                            }
                        },
                    )
                finally:
                    # Crucially, delete the message from the source queue to prevent
                    # it from being processed again. This is done for both
                    # successful processing and after moving to the DLQ.
                    sqs_client.delete_message(
                        QueueUrl=source_queue_url,
                        ReceiptHandle=receipt_handle,
                    )
                    print(f"Deleted message {msg['MessageId']} from source queue.")

        except KeyboardInterrupt:
            print("Shutting down consumer.")
            break
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"An unexpected error occurred: {e}")
            # In a real-world scenario, you might want more robust error handling
            time.sleep(5)


def send_test_messages(source_queue_url, aws_region="us-east-1"):
    """Helper function to send one successful and one failing message."""
    sqs_client = boto3.client("sqs", region_name=aws_region)
    
    # A message that should be processed successfully
    sqs_client.send_message(
        QueueUrl=source_queue_url,
        MessageBody=json.dumps({"id": "msg-001", "status": "ok", "data": "some payload"})
    )
    
    # A message that is designed to fail processing
    sqs_client.send_message(
        QueueUrl=source_queue_url,
        MessageBody=json.dumps({"id": "msg-002", "status": "fail", "data": "bad payload"})
    )
    print(f"Sent two test messages to {source_queue_url}")


# To run this code, you need to have two SQS queues created in your AWS account
# and set the following environment variables.
# AWS credentials must be configured (e.g., via ~/.aws/credentials or IAM role).
